hi!! going to look at a used e-bike saturday. what should i check before buying? battery health and range mostly..

bike got stolen outside the library and ive been saving for a replacement, been on the shuttle bus and rides from kenji since. kenji drove me to chem again today in his hatchback 🫠 so id really like to stop mooching lol

Good plan, and sorry about the stolen bike. The battery is the most expensive part, so start there. Here's a rundown:

**Battery and range**
- Ask the seller for the battery's age and how many charge cycles it has had. Most last about 500-1,000 cycles.
- Ask for the real-world range on one charge, then compare it to the manufacturer's claim. A big gap means a worn battery.
- Look for swelling, cracks, rust on the contacts, or a case that has been opened.
- Make sure it charges. Ask them to show it charging, and check that the charger fits and isn't a knockoff.
- On the display, check that the battery bars drop gradually. Fast drops under load mean weak cells.

**Motor and ride**
- Test ride for at least 10-15 minutes, including a hill if you can.
- Listen for grinding or clicking. Check that the assist engages smoothly with no jerking.
- Try every assist level.

**Frame and parts**
- Look for cracks near the welds and the battery mount.
- Check the brakes, tire wear, chain wear and wobble in the wheels.
- Spin the pedals and check the gears shift cleanly.

**Paperwork**
- Get the brand and model so you can look up the original price.
- Ask for the receipt or proof of ownership. Since yours was stolen, you really don't want to buy a stolen bike.
- Ask about warranty transfer, if there is one.

Want me to turn this into a shorter checklist you can run through on the spot?
yes pls!! too long lol. just bullets i can go thru in order at the seller's place

Here's the short version, in the order to do it:

**Before the ride (5 min)**
- [ ] Battery case: no swelling, cracks or rust
- [ ] Ask: battery age and charge cycles?
- [ ] Ask: real range on one charge?
- [ ] Receipt or proof of ownership
- [ ] Brand and model (look up the price later)

**Test ride (10-15 min)**
- [ ] Battery charge level at start, then again at the end. How much did it drop?
- [ ] Try every assist level
- [ ] Assist engages smoothly
- [ ] No grinding or clicking from the motor
- [ ] Brakes grab evenly
- [ ] Gears shift cleanly
- [ ] Ride a hill if one is nearby

**After the ride (5 min)**
- [ ] Plug it in and confirm it charges
- [ ] Check wheels for wobble and tires for wear
- [ ] Check the frame for cracks near welds
- [ ] Take photos of the serial number

If anything fails, use it to negotiate the price down or walk away. Good luck on Saturday!
